deck: A local-first multimodal robotic companion and scientific tool-routing benchmark ecosystem for large tool registries (N = 20–100). Features sub-6ms FastEmbed semantic reflexes for physical kinematics and hardware safety, a filtered Layer 2 decision layer combining FAISS candidate pruning with the zero-token LAYA cross-encoder (95.8% accuracy), stateful LangGraph execution with dual-layer PostgreSQL memory (PostgresSaver + Mem0 pgvector), and foundational DINOv3 vision with Bidirectional A* navigation.

projectDetails.name: MoKa AI Assistant & Tool-Routing Benchmark Ecosystem
projectDetails.institution: FH Campus Wien · Autonomous AI Systems

projectDetails.summary: A hybrid embodied AI companion and empirical research evaluation suite. Designed for dual deployment on physical Anki Cozmo hardware and 100% hardware-free in simulation, MoKa implements a two-tier cognitive routing pipeline: Layer 1 sub-6ms FastEmbed semantic reflexes for real-time motor kinematics and safety halts, paired with a Layer 2 filtered cognitive decision layer combining FAISS Top-k Tool RAG with the 135M parameter LAYA cross-encoder (95.8% accuracy, 0 generative output tokens) or local Ollama LLMs (qwen2.5:3b). Backed by dual-layer PostgreSQL persistence (PostgresSaver connection pooling + Mem0 pgvector memory reconciliation), Silero VAD / Kokoro-ONNX neural speech, and DINOv3 vision with sub-35ms Bidirectional A* path planning.
projectDetails.problem: Conventional embodied LLM assistants suffer from 1.5s+ reasoning latency, prompt pre-fill explosion (O(N) token bloat) as tool catalogs scale (20 to 100+ tools), softmax attention dilution / hallucination on semantically adjacent tools, lack of decoupled hardware safety halts, and cloud telemetry dependencies for physical robot interactions.
projectDetails.solution: Architected a decoupled two-tier routing and control hierarchy: Tier 1 sub-6ms FastEmbed semantic reflexes for instant motor kinematics and system commands; Tier 2 bounded O(k) FAISS candidate pruning feeding the lightweight 135M parameter LAYA cross-encoder (eliminating output tokens) or local Ollama; persistent dual-tier PostgreSQL memory (PostgresSaver checkpoints + Mem0 pgvector biographical profile with few-shot reconciliation); DINOv3 foundational vision with SVD PCA heatmaps; and hardware ReflexSafetyGuard with sub-35ms Bidirectional A* planning.
projectDetails.architectureDescription: Two-Tier Fallback Hierarchy: Layer 1 Semantic Router (FastEmbed bge-small-en-v1.5) directly executes PyCozmo motor actions & system utilities in 5.5ms (0 tokens); Layer 2 routes complex multi-step reasoning through FAISS Top-k (k=3) candidate pruning into the 135M LAYA typed decision cross-encoder (95.8% accuracy, 0 output tokens) or local Ollama qwen2.5:3b. Stateful execution is orchestrated by LangGraph with dual-layer PostgreSQL memory (PostgresSaver connection pooling + Mem0 pgvector long-term profile), Kokoro-ONNX voice synthesis, and DINOv3 vision with Bidirectional A* motion planning.

chapters.title: The Two-Tier Reflex Hierarchy
chapters.subtitle: Sub-6ms Semantic Reflexes & Hardware Safety Interceptor
chapters.content: Physical robotic assistants cannot afford the 1,500ms+ latency of standard LLM reasoning loops for motor safety. MoKa implements a Layer 1 FastEmbed semantic router (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) executing in 5.5ms (median P50), intercepting physical kinematics, emergency halts, and system utilities with 0 LLM tokens and 100% accuracy on physical commands. Completely decoupled from host AI lag, the ReflexSafetyGuard intercepts PyCozmo motor methods, monitoring 4 infrared cliff sensors, desk pick-up, upward pitch bumps (>20° / 0.35 rad), deceleration shocks (<-2200 mm/s²), and camera visual motion stasis to halt motors in <10ms and trigger autonomous evasive maneuvers before table falls or motor stalls occur.
highlights: 5.5ms median reflex path (over 200x faster than LLM)
100% accuracy on physical robot movement commands
<10ms hardware cliff cut & event-driven motor interception
Sliding-window accelerometer shock & OpenCV visual stasis detection

chapters.title: Scalable Tool Routing & LangGraph
chapters.subtitle: FAISS Top-k Pruning & Zero-Token LAYA Cross-Encoder
chapters.content: In conventional LLM architectures, passing 15 to 100+ tool schemas into a monolithic prompt degrades classification accuracy, bloats prompt pre-fill latency to 2,000–8,000ms, and causes softmax attention dilution (dropping monolithic LAYA to 60.4%). MoKa solves this via a Two-Layer Top-K architecture: an in-memory FAISS vector index with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 pre-filters the catalog to top-k (k=3) candidates, reducing input complexity to O(k) constant space. The pruned choices are evaluated by the 135M parameter LAYA cross-encoder (convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions), achieving 95.8% Top-1 accuracy with 0 generative output tokens—matching local Ollama qwen2.5:3b while slashing mean latency from 1,455.6ms to 205.3ms.
highlights: 95.8% routing accuracy (matching 3B LLM, +8.3% over monolithic baseline)
0 generative output tokens via 135M LAYA cross-encoder
O(k) constant context complexity scaling across 20 to 100 tools

chapters.title: Dual-Tier Memory & Multimodal Voice
chapters.subtitle: Pooled PostgresSaver Checkpoints & Mem0 pgvector Reconciliation
chapters.content: MoKa maintains contextual continuity without cloud lock-in through a dual memory substrate. Short-term dialogue threads are preserved via LangGraph PostgresSaver backed by an auto-reconnecting psycopg3 connection pool that effortlessly survives serverless scale-to-zero idle disconnects on Neon. When sessions exceed 6 turns, older messages are summarized and pruned via RemoveMessage, bounding context bloat. Long-term biographical facts are managed by Mem0 backed by PostgreSQL pgvector (collection moka_user_memories, 384-D FastEmbed vectors), featuring an Intelligent Memory Reconciliation engine that runs few-shot dialogue evaluation to execute in-place UPDATEs, explicit DELETEs (forgetting negated facts), and ADDs, synchronized two-way with user_profile.md. Multimodal voice pairs Silero VAD (250ms silence threshold) with faster-whisper and Kokoro-ONNX 24kHz neural synthesis, executing conversational barge-in with sub-50ms audio queue flushing.
highlights: Resilient Neon PostgreSQL connection pool surviving serverless idle disconnections
Mem0 pgvector persistent profile with intelligent UPDATE/DELETE/ADD reconciliation
Rolling summarizer pruning active history beyond 6 messages via RemoveMessage
Silero VAD + faster-whisper + Kokoro-ONNX TTS with <50ms conversational barge-in

chapters.title: Cyber-Physical Perception & Path Planning
chapters.subtitle: Foundational DINOv3 Vision & Sub-35ms Bidirectional A*
chapters.content: Embodied desktop robotics requires spatial awareness and robust navigation under real-world track slip and lighting variations. MoKa integrates a foundational DINOv3 Vision Transformer backbone extracting 384-dimensional dense patch embeddings at >=15 FPS. A TemporalDebouncer verifies visual landmarks across 3 consecutive frames (cosine similarity > 0.75) to anchor features in Landmark SLAM, compensating for odometry drift. Motion planning runs over a 10mm discretized 2D occupancy grid using a Bidirectional A* search algorithm: expanding frontiers simultaneously from Cozmo's start pose and the charger pre-dock approach point, reducing state-space complexity to O(b^(d/2)) and converging in <35ms with a strict 50mm obstacle buffer. The system seamlessly degrades to simulated autonomy (--dry-run and --source webcam) when physical hardware is detached.
chapters.codeSnippet:
# Sub-35ms Bidirectional A* Motion Planning with 50mm Safety Clearance
def plan_bidirectional_astar(start: Tuple[float, float], goal: Tuple[float, float],
                             obstacles: List[BlockObstacle]) -> PathPlanningResult:
    # Inflate blocks with 50mm safety buffer + robot track radius (35mm)
    grid = OccupancyGrid(resolution_mm=10.0, clearance_mm=50.0 + 35.0)
    grid.rasterize_obstacles(obstacles)
    
    # Simultaneous forward & backward search -> O(b^(d/2)) convergence (<35ms)
    forward_frontier, backward_frontier = PriorityQueue(), PriorityQueue()
    intersect_node = search_frontiers(forward_frontier, backward_frontier, grid)
    
    smooth_waypoints = decimate_string_pulling(reconstruct_path(intersect_node))
    return PathPlanningResult(success=True, waypoints=smooth_waypoints)
highlights: DINOv3 ViT dense 384-D patch embeddings at >=15 FPS with SVD PCA heatmaps
TemporalDebouncer (3-frame verification) & Landmark SLAM drift compensation
Sub-35ms Bidirectional A* path planning over 10mm grid with 50mm safety clearance
100% hardware-free execution via simulation dry-run & webcam fallback
